region: Vila Nova de Gaia · Porto and Douro, Portugal
about: Taylor’s, known in the United States as Taylor Fladgate, is one of the oldest Port houses. Job Bearsley founded it in 1692 in Vila Nova de Gaia, across the Douro River from Porto, and its full name comes from the 1838 partnership of Joseph Taylor, John Alexander Fladgate and Morgan Yeatman. The house is credited with creating the Late Bottled Vintage style, and it now sits within a group that also includes Fonseca and Croft.

Fine Ruby is the house’s youngest, most fruit-driven style. Wines from the upper Douro Valley, from native grapes including Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz, Tinta Barroca, Tinto Cão and Tinta Amarela, are fortified with grape spirit partway through fermentation, which stops the yeast and keeps the grapes’ natural sweetness. The young wines then age for two to three years in large oak vats in Taylor’s lodges in Gaia, where they are blended for balance and a consistent house style and bottled ready to drink.

Taylor’s describes concentrated blackcurrant and cherry on the nose and a full-bodied, firm palate of black fruit. Its US importer, Kobrand, lists about 97 grams per liter of residual sugar at 20 percent alcohol, carried by supple tannins. It needs no decanting; the house suggests serving it at 16 to 18 °C, a little below room temperature, with blue cheese, berries or dark chocolate.
